title: Reflection at Curved Mirrors — 40 MCQs
description: Mirror formula relating object distance, image distance and focal length; relation between object size and image size (linear magnification); real and virtual images in geometrical optics; and calculation of the focal length and radius of curvature of curved mirrors with their applications.

questions.q: For a spherical mirror, the relation between the object distance u, the image distance v and the focal length f (real-is-positive convention) is
questions.explanation: The mirror formula is 1/u + 1/v = 1/f, where u, v and f are all measured from the pole of the mirror.

questions.q: The focal length f of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature R by
questions.explanation: The principal focus lies midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so f = R/2; for a plane mirror R is infinite and hence f is infinite.

questions.q: The linear magnification m produced by a spherical mirror is given by
questions.explanation: Magnification is the ratio of the image size to the object size, and it is also equal to −v/u, the negative sign showing that a real image is inverted.

questions.q: The image formed by a convex mirror of an object placed anywhere in front of it is always
options: real, erect and of the same size
questions.explanation: A convex mirror diverges the reflected rays, so the image is always formed behind the mirror; it is virtual, erect and smaller than the object.

questions.q: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles mainly because they
options: form a magnified real image of the traffic behind
form an erect, diminished image and therefore give a wide field of view
form an image which can be taken on a screen
have a very short focal length and a small field of view
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always gives an erect, diminished virtual image, so a large region behind the vehicle can be seen in a small mirror.

questions.q: A real image formed by a concave mirror
options: is always of the same size as the object
is always formed behind the mirror
can be obtained on a screen and is inverted
cannot be obtained on a screen and is erect
questions.explanation: In a real image the reflected rays actually meet, so it can be caught on a screen; for a concave mirror such an image is inverted.

questions.q: A dentist uses a concave mirror to see a magnified image of a tooth. For this the tooth is held
options: at the centre of curvature of the mirror
beyond the centre of curvature of the mirror
between the pole and the principal focus of the mirror
at the principal focus of the mirror
questions.explanation: When the object lies between the pole and the focus, a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect and magnified image, which is exactly what is needed to examine a tooth.

questions.q: The focal length of a plane mirror is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror has an infinite radius of curvature, and since f = R/2 its focal length is also infinite.

questions.q: The principal focus of a concave mirror is the point on the principal axis at which
options: a narrow beam of light parallel to the axis diverges after reflection
a narrow beam of light parallel to the axis converges after reflection
the incident ray is reflected back along its own path
the image of an object placed at infinity is virtual
questions.explanation: A concave mirror is converging, so paraxial rays parallel to the principal axis meet at the principal focus after reflection.

questions.q: When an object is placed at infinity in front of a concave mirror, the image is formed
options: at the focus and is real, inverted and highly diminished
at infinity and is highly magnified
at the centre of curvature and is of the same size
behind the mirror and is virtual and erect
questions.explanation: Rays from an object at infinity are parallel to the principal axis and are brought to a focus at F, giving a real, inverted and very small image.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a focal length of 10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm in front of it. The image is formed (real-is-positive convention)
options: 6 cm in front of the mirror
25 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm, i.e. a real image 30 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.q: A convex mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of it. The image is formed
options: 10 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: For a convex mirror f = −15 cm, so 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 − 1/30 = −1/10, giving v = −10 cm; the negative sign shows the image is 10 cm behind the mirror.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 20 cm forms a real image of an object placed 25 cm in front of it. The image distance is
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/25 = (5 − 4)/100 = 1/100, so v = 100 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.q: An object placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror forms a real image 60 cm from the mirror. The focal length of the mirror is
An object placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror forms a real image at 20 cm from the mirror. The radius of curvature of the mirror is
A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm has an object placed 15 cm in front of it. The magnification produced by the mirror is
questions.explanation: v = 30 cm, so m = −v/u = −30/15 = −2; the negative sign shows a real, inverted image twice the size of the object.

questions.q: An object 4 cm high is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The height of the image is
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 30 × 10/20 = 15 cm, so m = −15/30 = −0.5 and the image height is 0.5 × 4 = 2 cm, inverted.

questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. The magnification of the image is
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 30 × (−15)/(30 + 15) = −10 cm, so m = −v/u = 10/30 = +1/3; the image is virtual, erect and one-third the size of the object.

questions.q: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
options: at the centre of curvature, real, inverted and of the same size as the object
at the focus, real, inverted and diminished
at infinity, real and highly magnified
behind the mirror, virtual and erect
questions.explanation: When u = R = 2f, the mirror formula gives v = 2f = R, so the image is formed at the centre of curvature itself; the magnification is −1, i.e. the image is inverted and of the same size.

questions.q: Which type of spherical mirror can form both real and virtual images?
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a real image when the object is beyond the focus and a virtual image when the object lies between the pole and the focus; a convex mirror always gives a virtual image.

questions.q: When an object is placed at the principal focus of a concave mirror, the image is formed
questions.explanation: For u = f, 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 0, so v is infinite; the reflected rays emerge parallel and the image is formed at infinity.

questions.q: An object is placed between the pole and the principal focus of a concave mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: For an object between the pole and the focus the reflected rays diverge, so the image is virtual and erect; the mirror formula gives a magnification greater than 1.

questions.q: Which of the following is true of a virtual image?
options: It can be obtained on a screen and is always inverted
It is always of the same size as the object
It is always formed by a convex lens
It cannot be obtained on a screen and is always erect
questions.explanation: In a virtual image the reflected rays only appear to meet, so the image cannot be caught on a screen; it is erect and lies behind the mirror.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm has an object placed 20 cm in front of it. The image is formed at a distance of
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/15 − 1/20 = (4 − 3)/60 = 1/60, so v = 60 cm; the image is real, inverted and three times as large as the object.

questions.q: An object 6 cm high is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The height of the image is
questions.explanation: v = 15 × 10/(15 − 10) = 30 cm, so m = −30/15 = −2 and the image height is 2 × 6 = 12 cm, inverted.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a focal length of 12 cm. An object is placed only 6 cm in front of it. The image formed is
options: 12 cm in front of the mirror
4 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 6 × 12/(6 − 12) = −12 cm; the negative sign shows a virtual image 12 cm behind the mirror, erect and twice as large as the object.

questions.q: An object is placed 12 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 8 cm. The image distance and magnification are
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24, so v = 24 cm and m = −v/u = −24/12 = −2; the image is real, inverted and twice as large.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 48 cm. An object is placed 36 cm in front of it. The image is formed at
questions.explanation: f = R/2 = 24 cm, so 1/v = 1/24 − 1/36 = (3 − 2)/72 = 1/72 and v = 72 cm; the image is real and inverted.

questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is
options: virtual, 6.7 cm behind the mirror and half the size of the object
real, 30 cm in front of the mirror and three times as large as the object
real, 20 cm in front of the mirror and twice as large as the object
virtual, 20 cm behind the mirror and twice as large as the object
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 10 × 20/(10 − 20) = −20 cm, so the image is 20 cm behind the mirror; m = −v/u = +2, i.e. virtual, erect and twice as large.

questions.q: An object is placed 6 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 12 cm. The image is formed
options: 4 cm in front of the mirror and is two-thirds the size of the object
4 cm behind the mirror and is two-thirds the size of the object
3 cm behind the mirror and is half the size of the object
12 cm behind the mirror and is twice the size of the object
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 6 × (−12)/(6 + 12) = −4 cm, so the image is 4 cm behind the mirror; m = −v/u = 4/6 = +2/3.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 12 cm forms a virtual image three times as large as the object. The object distance is
questions.explanation: For a virtual, erect image m = +3, so v = −3u. Then 1/u − 1/(3u) = 1/12 gives 2/(3u) = 1/12, so u = 8 cm.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm is to form a real image three times as large as the object. The object must be placed at a distance of
questions.explanation: For a real image m = −3, so v = 3u. Then 1/u + 1/(3u) = 1/15 gives 4/(3u) = 1/15, so u = 20 cm and v = 60 cm.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms a real image twice as large as the object. The object distance is
questions.explanation: For a real image m = −2, so v = 2u. Then 1/u + 1/(2u) = 1/10 gives 3/(2u) = 1/10, so u = 15 cm.

questions.q: An object placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror forms a real image 30 cm from the mirror. The radius of curvature of the mirror is
An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 10 cm. The image is
options: 5 cm in front of the mirror and half the size of the object
20 cm behind the mirror and twice the size of the object
5 cm behind the mirror and half the size of the object
10 cm behind the mirror and of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 10 × (−10)/(10 + 10) = −5 cm, so the image is 5 cm behind the mirror; m = −v/u = 5/10 = +0.5.

questions.q: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 40 cm. The image formed is
options: virtual, 40 cm behind the mirror and twice as large as the object
real, 40 cm in front of the mirror and twice as large as the object
real, 60 cm in front of the mirror and three times as large as the object
virtual, 13.3 cm behind the mirror and two-thirds the size of the object
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 20 × 40/(20 − 40) = −40 cm, so the image is 40 cm behind the mirror; m = −v/u = +2, i.e. virtual, erect and magnified twice.

questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. The magnification of the image is
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 10 × (−15)/(10 + 15) = −6 cm, so m = −v/u = 6/10 = +0.6; the image is virtual, erect and diminished.

A convex mirror forms an image one-fourth the size of an object placed 30 cm in front of it. The radius of curvature of the mirror is
An object 2 cm high is placed 18 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. The image is
questions.explanation: v = 18 × 12/(18 − 12) = 36 cm, so m = −36/18 = −2; the image height is 2 × 2 = 4 cm and the negative sign shows it is inverted and real.
